title: Why Inheritance?
summary: Understand what inheritance is, why it exists, and how parent and child classes let you reuse code cleanly without copy-pasting.
learningObjectives: Understand what inheritance means in simple plain English
Identify why copying and pasting code across related classes causes problems
Distinguish between a parent class and a child class
Understand how the extends keyword connects a child class to a parent class
Observe how a child class can call methods written inside the parent class
expectedOutcomes: Ability to explain what inheritance is and why we use it without confusing jargon
Confidence to create a simple parent class and child class in Java using extends

activities.title: The Family Traits and Blueprint Analogy
activities.content:
Think about human families. Children inherit traits from their parents, like eye color, hair texture, or height. The child doesn't have to create those traits from scratch—they get them naturally from their parents! At the same time, the child can learn new unique skills, like playing the piano or speaking Spanish, which the parents might not have.

In Java, inheritance works the exact same way:
- A **parent class** defines shared traits and behaviors (like having a name and being able to eat).
- A **child class** inherits those shared traits automatically and adds its own unique abilities (like barking or flying).

You write the shared code once in the parent class, and all child classes inherit it immediately!

activities.title: What Is Inheritance and Why Does It Exist?
Before vs After Inheritance: Eliminating Duplication
activities.description: See the exact difference between repetitive code without inheritance and clean code with inheritance.

steps.description: Notice how BadDog and BadCat both declared 'String name' and 'void eat()'. This duplicated code creates maintenance headaches.
We create a parent class 'Animal' containing the common field 'name' and the shared methods 'eat()' and 'sleep()'.
We write 'class Dog extends Animal'. The 'extends' keyword makes Dog a child of Animal. Dog inherits name, eat(), and sleep().
Inside Dog, we only write 'void bark()'. Dog does not need to repeat eat() or sleep()!
In main(), we create a Dog object. Notice that myDog.eat() works smoothly even though eat() was written inside Animal.

activities.title: Adding a New Class in Seconds: The Power of Reusability
activities.description: Observe how easy it is to add a third animal (Bird) to the zoo when you have an Animal parent class.

steps.description: We have the existing Animal parent class with 'name', 'age', and 'eat()'.
To add a Bird, we write 'class Bird extends Animal'. We do not have to write name, age, or eat() again.
We add the unique method 'fly()' specifically for Bird.
When we instantiate Bird, it has full access to both Animal properties and Bird abilities.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of inheritance in Java?
options: To prevent classes from having any variables
To allow one class to reuse fields and methods from another class
To run Java programs faster by skipping the compiler
To force all classes to be written in a single file
questions.explanation: Inheritance allows a child class to inherit fields and methods from a parent class, avoiding duplicate code and promoting reusability.

questions.question: Which Java keyword is used by a child class to inherit from a parent class?
options: implements
inherits
extends
imports
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword is used in Java when a class inherits from another class (e.g., class Dog extends Animal).

questions.question: If class Dog extends Animal, which class is the parent (superclass)?
options: Dog
Animal
Both are parents
Neither is a parent
questions.explanation: Animal is the parent (superclass) and Dog is the child (subclass).

questions.question: What does the DRY principle stand for in programming?
options: Do Run Yesterday
Don't Repeat Yourself
Data Recording Yield
Design Rules Yearly
questions.explanation: DRY stands for 'Don't Repeat Yourself', which means avoiding duplicated code by centralizing shared logic.

questions.question: Suppose Animal has a method void eat(). If Dog extends Animal, can a Dog object call eat()?
options: No, because eat() is not written inside the Dog class
Yes, because Dog inherits accessible methods from Animal
Only if eat() is rewritten inside Dog
Only if Dog creates an Animal object inside eat()
questions.explanation: Because Dog extends Animal, Dog inherits all accessible methods from Animal, including eat().

questions.question: Where do shared fields and methods belong in an inheritance hierarchy?
options: In every child class separately
In the parent class
In a separate unrelated utility file
Only in the main method
questions.explanation: Shared fields and methods move up into the parent class so all child classes can reuse them.

questions.question: Can a child class have its own unique methods in addition to inherited methods?
options: No, a child class can only contain what the parent has
Yes, a child class can add its own new fields and methods
Only if the parent gives explicit written permission
Only if the child has no fields
questions.explanation: A child class inherits everything visible from the parent AND can add its own unique fields and methods.

questions.question: If Cat extends Animal and adds meow(), can an instance of Animal call meow()?
options: Yes, parents can call all methods of their children
No, inheritance flows downward; a parent class knows nothing about methods added by its child
Yes, if meow() is static
Yes, if Cat is instantiated first
questions.explanation: Inheritance flows downward. A parent class does NOT know about unique methods declared in its subclasses.

questions.question: What happens if you fix a bug in a method inside the parent class?
options: All child classes automatically get the bug fix without modifying child code
You have to manually update every child class file
The program will crash until child classes are re-compiled with new names
Child classes keep running the old buggy code forever
questions.explanation: Because the logic lives in the parent class, fixing it in the parent immediately fixes it for all child classes!

questions.question: When you execute 'Dog dog = new Dog();', how many objects are created in heap memory?
options: Two objects: one Animal object and one Dog object
One object: a Dog object that contains both Animal and Dog fields
Zero objects until a method is called
Three objects including the String class
questions.explanation: Only one unified object is created on the heap: the Dog instance, which internally includes space for inherited Animal fields.

interviewQA.question: What is inheritance in Java and what primary problem does it solve?
interviewQA.answer: Inheritance is a fundamental OOP mechanism where a new class (subclass/child) acquires the fields and methods of an existing class (superclass/parent). It solves the problem of code duplication by allowing shared state and behaviors to be written once in a base class, adhering to the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle.

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between a superclass and a subclass?
interviewQA.answer: A superclass (or parent class) is the general class whose properties and methods are inherited. A subclass (or child class) is the specialized class that extends the superclass, inheriting its visible members and adding new fields or methods specific to itself.

interviewQA.question: Does a child class create two separate objects in memory when instantiated?
interviewQA.answer: No. When you instantiate a child class with 'new Child()', only ONE object is created on the heap. That single object contains all fields defined in the child class along with all fields inherited from the parent class.

interviewQA.question: Can a parent class access methods defined only in its child class?
interviewQA.answer: No. Inheritance flows downward from parent to child. The parent class has no knowledge of any unique fields or methods declared in its subclasses.

interviewQA.question: What keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
interviewQA.answer: In Java, the 'extends' keyword is used to inherit a class (e.g., 'class Dog extends Animal').

interviewQA.question: Why is copy-pasting code across related classes considered bad practice?
interviewQA.answer: Copy-pasting code leads to bug proliferation, maintenance headaches, and inconsistent behavior. If logic needs to change or a bug is discovered, every duplicated copy must be located and modified individually, which is error-prone.

activities.title: 10-Point Mastery Checklist: Why Inheritance?
checklist: I can explain what inheritance is in simple words without academic jargon
I can identify what a parent class (superclass) is
I can identify what a child class (subclass) is
I know what the extends keyword does in Java
I can explain how inheritance eliminates duplicate code
I understand the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle
I know that calling an inherited method executes code defined in the parent class
I understand that a child class can add its own unique fields and methods
I understand that a parent class cannot access child-specific methods
I know that instantiating a child creates a single combined object on the heap

practiceProblems.title: Creating Your First Inheritance Relationship
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create a parent class named `Vehicle` with a field `String brand` and a method `void start()` that prints `brand + " is starting..."`.
Then create a child class named `Car` that extends `Vehicle` and adds a method `void honk()` that prints `"Beep beep!"`.
In the main method of `Main`, create a `Car` object, set its `brand` to `"Toyota"`, call `start()`, and then call `honk()`.
hints: Use 'class Car extends Vehicle' to establish inheritance.
Remember that 'car.brand' is inherited from Vehicle, so you can set it directly.

practiceProblems.title: Zoo Animal Hierarchy From Scratch
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Buddy is eating food.
Buddy says Woof!
Whiskers is eating food.
Whiskers says Meow!
hints: Both Dog and Cat should inherit from Animal using the extends keyword.
Set the 'name' field on each instance before calling the methods.

practiceProblems.title: Employee and Developer Role Modeling
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Create a parent class `Employee` with fields `String name` and `double salary`, and a method `void showDetails()` that prints `"Employee: " + name + ", Salary: $" + salary`.
Create a child class `Developer` that extends `Employee`, adds a field `String primaryLanguage`, and a method `void writeCode()` that prints `name + " is writing code in " + primaryLanguage`.
In `Main.main()`, create a `Developer` object with name `"Alice"`, salary `85000.0`, and primary language `"Java"`. Call `showDetails()` followed by `writeCode()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Employee: Alice, Salary: $85000.0
Alice is writing code in Java
hints: Developer inherits name and salary from Employee.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Missing Extends and Redundant Methods
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The following program was written by a beginner who attempted to create a parent `Device` class and a child `SmartPhone` class. However, the code does not compile because the relationship is missing, and the developer duplicated fields unnecessarily. Fix the code so `SmartPhone` properly inherits from `Device` without duplicating `brand` or `turnOn()`, and prints the expected output.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Pixel device is now ON
Calling 555-0199 from Pixel
hints: Add 'extends Device' to the declaration of SmartPhone.
Delete the redundant brand field and turnOn() method from SmartPhone.
